87ae7757cc5d.sentence: Every message to a session — a brief, a landing's red, a round, `watch tell` and `watch restart`, a comment — goes through that session's outbox, one record of who it was from, the line typed, and how it went: `typed` (a brief), `submitted` (it started a turn), `queued` (it waits behind the running turn), `brief` (written into a brief still to be typed), `not_typed` (the harness was not up, the terminal gone, Orca refused), or `missed` (typed, it started no turn and none runs: a dialog took it). Nothing is typed before the harness is up, nor ahead of the brief.

87b6220ba84c.sentence: A cut no longer needs a tap token on the host: only `gh` logged in as a user who may push factorium and dispatch the tap's workflow.

891c045bcd15.sentence: `issue comment` records the comment and reaches the live worker on the issue at once, through the same outbox as `watch tell`, never stopping its running turn: a working worker gets one line typed at its session (`delivery: submitted`, `queued`, or `missed`); one whose brief is not yet handed gets it in that brief (`brief`); a waiting one is not typed at, its watch episode carries it (`watch`); with no worker, or when delivery fails (`undelivered` says why), `none`. The next brief carries every comment.

8c3d7e463594.sentence: No crate has unit or doc tests (`[lib] test = false`; `checks.sh` fails one in `crates/domain`). The effect crates' tests (`crates/host/tests`, `crates/harness/tests`) hold only their edge: the real program, file or process.
8c3d7e463594.why: how factorium's own tests are written, not what factorium does for a user; held by checks.sh and the scenarios' fixture

8c88e1798a4d.sentence: A repo factorium manages has its base moved only by promotion; anything else that moves the base turns promotion red.

8d14bdd7a59e.sentence: One resident agent session, the watch, deals with every finding: escalations, failed, hot and silent workers, red promotions, red idle work, failed cuts, resource holds.
8d14bdd7a59e.why: restates a registered promise beside it (admission-from-readings, shortest-hold-first, off-path-to-watch, no-finding-unlooked, idle-gives-way)

91db289c1891.summary: truefit.toml was changed by 4 fixes in 180 days, and no registered promise's check covers it
91db289c1891.why: truefit.toml is the check ladder's own registry, not code that keeps a promise: these fixes added the worktrees and line models with their covers (factorium#187, #188, #189) and moved each model's commit to the one it describes. The promises those models keep (WorkNeverLost, OneOwner, a landing at most once, ...) are checked by those models against the code they cover; the config's edits are bookkeeping of that, with no behaviour of their own to check.

921e1ee70fef.sentence: Its fast gate, which runs on every landing, spent 65 of its 138 seconds in Flux (measured on afkconvoy's gate when factorium was specified, 2026-11-17). factorium's rules are already held by its scenarios, run on the real binary, and by each change's mutants ([ADR 0032](0032-tests-only-at-the-outermost-layer.md)).
921e1ee70fef.why: context, evidence or a reopen condition, not behaviour a check can hold

926c047b4d0d.sentence: Which host installs factorium, and when (factorium#269): a host one of whose checkouts declares the cut of the daemon's own formula (its base, as last fetched, names it in `[cut]`) installs it at that cut, and only then; every other host's daemon, Homebrew's, upgrades its formula from the tap itself, each `upgrade_every` (an hour) since its last try, while no line move runs beside the ticks: `brew update`, then `brew upgrade`, on a thread beside the ticks, recorded on the tick after it ended.

9278d176bd2b.sentence: Not in factorium: teams, roles kept by factorium (an issue, or a checkout as its default, may name a role directory, §1.2–1.3, and that is all), workflows, stages, verdicts, rework, consults, patrols, intake and flow labels; GitHub in every form (tracker, pull requests, checks, branch protection, quota, Discussions); the daybook; the panel; batched rounds and the pairing tree; several hosts (remote claims, a shared proving branch, cross-host reports: `issue move`, §4, is not that, for no state is shared between hosts and nothing is read from the other host afterwards: one owner command hands one issue over by filing it there); Jira deliveries; the asking session; remote refs as state; caches as state.
9278d176bd2b.why: a description of the design, its scope or of another system (sunfmin/homebrew-tap, afkconvoy), not a promise a run of factorium could break

941db9f0ac35.sentence: A look (no model) every five minutes reads doctor's findings.
941db9f0ac35.why: restates a registered promise beside it (admission-from-readings, shortest-hold-first, off-path-to-watch, no-finding-unlooked, idle-gives-way)

946dbe0dbd8b.sentence: Its steps run beside the daemon's ticks as a promotion's slow gate does; the tag and the install follow on the tick after they ended, and the installed binary's proof (§4) runs beside the ticks too: the cut is recorded, made or failed with the proof's why, on the first tick after the proof ended, and until then none of the checkout's other moves is carried (factorium#242). A failed cut holds every later cut of its checkout until one of three: each tick reads it back and records it made once its tag and install hold; a cut by hand tries again; or a promotion moves the base to a commit other than the one it was cut from (the fix reaches the base only so), and the cut is owed again by the rule above.

972618f2a67f.sentence: A kept worktree that went bad is discarded on purpose with `issue start-over <checkout> <n> --why …`, only while no worker is on the issue: its uncommitted changes are committed, its branch is kept as `<branch>-abandoned`, a comment names that branch and the why, and the worktree goes, so the next start is branched from the proving tip.

9783fb8648a5.sentence: Only after the step passes does the daemon tag, `brew upgrade` (its tap already holds the new formula, published by the run it waited for) and prove the new binary before switching to it.

98d94faaae9a.sentence: Each reaches the worker at most once: the line `tell` or `restart` types is its delivery, nothing types it again, and a worker's own escalation is typed back at no one.

9a3f3bf5194f.sentence: The queue holds the busy share near the limit, and the load it holds back shows only in its wait, which admission reads.
9a3f3bf5194f.why: restates a registered promise beside it (admission-from-readings, shortest-hold-first, off-path-to-watch, no-finding-unlooked, idle-gives-way)

9b9c3f581a08.sentence: So each kind has at most one open issue, no kind waits on another, and once one closes the next run files the next of its kind.

a0277da0c989.sentence: What would reopen it: a landing that harms before review can catch it (secrets, data loss, something externally visible), and then a finding that holds promotion (`factorium hold`), not an approval on every landing; or measured evidence that findings after landing cost more than review before it.
a0277da0c989.why: context, evidence or a reopen condition, not behaviour a check can hold

a1bfd7edb63c.sentence: A repo on the host's checkout list: its path, base branch, proving branch, its **default role**, if any, and what the repo declares (§4). The default role is a role directory as for an issue (§1.3), by its absolute path, kept in the host's list and not in the repo's `factorium.toml`, since the path holds only on this host; it is named at `checkout add --role`, changed with `checkout edit --role` or taken away with `checkout edit --no-role`, each refused unless it is such a directory (factorium#249).

a2560e85b22b.sentence: It works by the rules of the factorium that runs: its session records which rules (their hash) it was briefed with, and a look that finds them other than the running binary's — a cut installed a version that changed them — closes that session between rounds, never in one, and starts a fresh one briefed with the new rules before the next round.

a2fc0e488c35.sentence: Its start goes before every other ready issue, held only by the memory and disk floors, never by the load.
a2fc0e488c35.why: ADR 0015 (urgent, rehomed from the old concepts table): the context line states the problem; the three decisions are held by tests/scenarios/urgent.rs

a7685f55d299.sentence: So does a line that stopped: whatever it owes is done within its bound or is a finding — a heavy queue that starts nothing past `stall_bound` (or whose oldest waits past `hold_bound` and `stall_bound` more), a landing no gate runs for past `stall_bound`, the oldest unpromoted landing past `promotion_bound` with no promotion running, the oldest uncut promotion past `cut_bound` with no cut running.

a7ad95898ed1.sentence: A crate over its target, or that grew at each of its last five landings that changed it, is a task: the idle tasks line runs `./lines.sh --tasks` after slimfit's `next`, and a `crate-lines` issue names the crate and the files that grew most (§1.16). Its worker deepens the crate; a target changes only with its reason in the issue that changes it.

a8f2a5921746.sentence: A **look** (no model) every five minutes, and on the next tick once a worker starts waiting for the watch, reads `doctor`'s findings; each condition is an **episode**, and an episode starts at most one **round**: a brief, an hour, and a report the watch files with `factorium watch report`. Escalations, failed workers, hot workers, red promotions, red idle work, failed cuts and resource holds all go to it.

a8ff180697da.sentence: A landing over its crate's target is green; the crate's growth is filed once, by idle work, not argued at every landing.
a8ff180697da.why: restates lines-never-fail and the idle tasks line's filing (ADR 0014)

aa1f9f891da1.sentence: Urgent is the owner's mark on an issue, never a worker's: `worker file` cannot set it.
aa1f9f891da1.why: ADR 0015 (urgent, rehomed from the old concepts table): the context line states the problem; the three decisions are held by tests/scenarios/urgent.rs

aae476d382e9.sentence: A crate's target is a trend, not a gate (factorium#163): `./lines.sh`, which `checks.sh` runs, prints each crate's lines against its target here and an overage, and never fails.

aae4e201ca85.sentence: Each start asks `stablehand pick`, counting factorium's own live sessions on each account, and starts the engine, model and account it answers, by the command stablehand keeps for that engine (`stablehand command set`); factorium adds only its own arguments, the guard and the session.
aae4e201ca85.why: how a start is made; its outcomes are the registered promises used-up-account-waits and without-stablehand-claude-code-alone

ac68931ab705.sentence: Any other conflict is red, naming every conflicting file (factorium#225).

ace2fb985724.sentence: One host-wide queue starts each when the host has room — by the same readings as admission, nothing else — never starves the oldest (it starts at once when nothing runs), starts one beside what runs only on a reading taken `heavy_settle` after the last start (so the load a start brings is read before the next), and ends one that holds others up past the hold bound.

af5afe10a864.summary: truefit.toml was changed by 4 fixes in 180 days, and no registered promise's check covers it
af5afe10a864.why: truefit.toml is truefit's own configuration, not code that keeps a promise: the fixes (factorium#186-189) only registered the line and worktrees models, named their covers, and moved each model's pinned commit. The promises those fixes keep are already registered with model checks (model line, line-live, worktrees) whose covers name the code they stand for.

afd8a2f2373a.sentence: The owner, 2026-11-22: 「把所有的工具都变成 universal。」「把公开的工具全部在 GitHub CI 上签。」「这个密钥的环境变量可以统一配置到账号上面吗？」 A personal account has no account-wide secrets; slimfit#100 put the one copy of them in sunfmin/homebrew-tap, whose `release` workflow signs every tool (its contract: the tap's `.github/workflows/README.md`).

b12fef398804.sentence: One whose answer is no JSON object, or not one as asked, is asked once more in the same session (Claude Code and Grok by `--resume`, agy by `--conversation`; Codex's session is ephemeral, so it is not), told only what was wrong and the one form the answer takes; both asks' time and tokens count, and the record says it was "answered as asked when asked again".
b12fef398804.why: restates a registered promise beside it (pick-within-bound, never-a-pick-without-picker) or the harness crate's asked tests

b3024e962d14.sentence: One with commits of its own, or checked out over changes not committed, is never reset: it is left, and is a doctor finding naming the checkout and how far behind it is.

b3bfe41e7545.sentence: Text is typed at a session only once its harness's own screen is up there: typed at a shell, a line is a command it runs.

b71544e4f2f6.sentence: A worker no second agent answers gets a refusal, never a pick of its own.
b71544e4f2f6.why: restates a registered promise beside it (pick-within-bound, never-a-pick-without-picker) or the harness crate's asked tests

b7f0f3769a08.sentence: No tick waits for a heavy run: every gate and step a tick starts runs beside the ticks.

b9a5917830e2.sentence: `slots = n`: n holders at most (1 is a mutex): a named resource, declared in the host's settings (`settings --resource <name> --slots <n> [--note <what it is>]`, `--remove`; a phone serves every checkout on the host, so no checkout's `factorium.toml` names it). `room`: as many as the host's readings allow: the resource `host`, which is never declared — the heavy queue, as below.

be311544eb70.sentence: A worker that dies, hangs or goes quiet, or a line that stops moving, tells nobody unless a check makes it a finding; one found while it only waits for what it was told to wait for spends the watch on nothing.
be311544eb70.why: an ADR's Context: why the decision was needed, not a promise of the system

bf18b78a3358.sentence: A daemon Homebrew installed notes its formula's link at start; once the link names another version (a cut by the daemon, by `factorium cut`, or by hand), it execs the link between ticks, as the same pid, once that binary is proven to open this host's database: it answers `doctor` on a copy (SQLite's backup, never the live file). A cut of the formula proves it right after the install; one that fails is a failed cut, its why the error and the copy's path (kept for a look), and the old binary runs on.

c2393ba1fe08.sentence: A change to the daemon's lifecycle (lock, exec, stop, liveness) edits `daemon/process.rs` only.
c2393ba1fe08.why: ADR 0005 describes the module split (which code lives where, what a change edits); none is behaviour a run could break

c29cc046c3d4.sentence: Not in factorium: teams, roles kept by factorium (an issue may name a role directory, §1.3, and that is all), workflows, stages, verdicts, rework, consults, patrols, intake and flow labels; GitHub in every form (tracker, pull requests, checks, branch protection, quota, Discussions); the daybook; the panel; batched rounds and the pairing tree; several hosts (remote claims, a shared proving branch, cross-host reports); Jira deliveries; the asking session; remote refs as state; caches as state.

c39ad7df5ff9.sentence: Each crate has a target for its source lines, so that one that only grows is seen and deepened.
c39ad7df5ff9.why: the ADR's context: why a target exists and why it is not a gate

c70957a90cc9.sentence: Claude Code's files say (each assistant message's `usage` once, by its id), Codex's (its last `token_count`), pi's (each assistant message's `usage`) and agy's (each `PLANNER_RESPONSE` of its `transcript.jsonl`: `input_tokens` and `cache_read_tokens` given, `output_tokens` written); DSH's, Kimi Code's and Grok's are not read, their tokens `null`. Each attempt also answers the role it started with, as `role` (`dir`, its directory, and `from`, `issue` or `checkout`, as `role_from` says, §3), and as `role_hash` a hash of what that role gave it, taken at its start: its rules and every file under its skills, read through the link, each file by its path under the skills and its bytes.

c85093d9125e.sentence: Claude Code, Codex, Grok and agy can be asked, each in a user directory of its own that holds only its login (agy's, its HOME, also an agent with no tools).
c85093d9125e.why: restates a registered promise beside it (pick-within-bound, never-a-pick-without-picker) or the harness crate's asked tests

c9fb8371b646.sentence: One binary, `factorium`. Three groups, by who uses them; the guard lets a worker run only `factorium worker …` and lets only the watch run `factorium watch …`.

cb730b2c89f0.sentence: Its merge is checked from `done` on, not only at its turn (§1.12, factorium#307). A branch that does not merge onto the proving tip is not the second red when the red before was one onto an older tip, which the branch now holds: proving moved since the worker merged what it was told (factorium#171). It is told as for a first red, with what landed since that tip and the files that conflict; past `moved_reds_max` of these in a row, it counts.

cd8736ddf529.sentence: It is recorded as any run is, its start beginning `every` again, and its tasks are filed by the same rule, so it never files a second open issue of a kind.

d14d1e374722.sentence: A store written by an older binary is read by a newer one as it is: no script is run by hand, so the swap's proof (§4) passes on it and the daemon moves to the newer binary by itself (factorium#270). The log is never rewritten; a change to what is kept is carried by the code that reads it.

d2507572d91f.sentence: A slow one, past half the hang bound (five `tick_every`, never under two minutes: a daemon silent that long is taken to hang), is kept, and for an hour is a finding naming how long it took and that step (factorium#231).

d38d1e5b2123.sentence: One of another checkout is `--blocked-by <checkout>#N`, met once it is closed (landed); `<checkout>#N@cut` is met only once a cut of that checkout holds its landing, and installed it where its `[cut]` names a formula, for a tool used from another repo.

d5c0f18234d3.sentence: A personal account has no account-wide secrets; slimfit#100 put the one copy of them in sunfmin/homebrew-tap, whose `release` workflow signs every tool (its contract: the tap's `.github/workflows/README.md`).
d5c0f18234d3.why: a description of the design, its scope or of another system (sunfmin/homebrew-tap, afkconvoy), not a promise a run of factorium could break

d5cdf980819b.sentence: An issue that names no role takes its checkout's default role (§1.2); an issue's own role always wins over it, and `issue show` answers the role the next worker starts with as `role`, and as `role_from` whether it is the issue's own (`issue`) or the checkout's (`checkout`). The role is named at `issue add --role` or at `issue edit --role` (changed, or taken away with `--no-role`), each refused unless it is such a directory; a worker already started keeps the directory it started in, each attempt after the edit starts with the role as edited, and the edit is a comment on the issue saying from what to what (factorium#248). An account is one of §1.7, refused at `issue add` unless this host can use it.

d6ba8bddf1db.sentence: Beside it doctor answers `asks`: every issue of every checkout that waits for a person (added `--waiting-for-human`, or left so by `issue wait-for-human`, the watch's or a session's), oldest first, each with its checkout and number, its title, its question (the first line of its body after any "Based on …" line), why, when it started waiting and who left it so.

d7337baf3f06.sentence: Only spending money is left to the owner, in the report's `human` part, which `doctor` shows.

d9626120c10c.sentence: The base branch is what every host and every release builds from, so nothing may reach it that a gate has not passed on that very tree, and a slow gate cannot run on every landing.
d9626120c10c.why: an ADR's context: why the decision was needed, no behaviour of factorium's

d9e140e70705.sentence: `./gate.sh`: fmt, clippy, the per-crate lines against their targets (shown, not held, [ADR 0031](docs/adr/0031-a-crate-s-line-target-is-a-trend-not-a-gate.md)), and the tests under `slimfit check`, which runs them once, instrumented, against `.slimfit/baseline.json` (no failures, no more uncovered lines, tests no slower than the baseline allows; [ADR 0032](docs/adr/0032-tests-only-at-the-outermost-layer.md)).
d9e140e70705.why: says what ./gate.sh runs; gate.sh and slimfit check --help say it

dab3e8e2ad2f.sentence: The rules are those of the daemon that runs, set as it starts (a newer binary swapped to, or an older one a rollback went back to), never by another process that asks: a newer binary whose proof failed does not run the daemon, which would else be refused its own gates (factorium#241). A waiter of an older binary is refused, and execs the installed one (its own binary found before it waits, so an upgrade meanwhile does not hide it), keeping its place; an entry waiting under replaced rules is passed over until its asker asks again under the daemon's, so it holds none up.

dad9071fb3d9.sentence: **Every checkout has a proving branch**: one path.

dda2f7aebfb2.sentence: A new event kind may be written first by any process of the version that adds it, a CLI call before the daemon swapped among them: a daemon of an older version whose store cannot read it fails its ticks, and a failed tick still starts that proof and swaps once it passed (not while a line move runs beside the ticks), since the newer binary alone reads the store; a rollback's kept binary is gone back to only when no link to swap to is proven (factorium#252). A cut of the formula proves it right after the install (the daemon's cut beside its ticks, recorded on the tick after the proof ended); one that fails is a failed cut, its why the error and the copy's path (kept for a look), and the old binary runs on.

df05ad7bce8a.sentence: A session typed at beside the ticks is not tried again by a look until that ended; the daemon lets it end before it stops, and swaps to a new binary only once none runs (factorium#311). A prompt Claude Code took is read from its session file as typed, or in the block it writes a long paste in (`<pasted_content id="…">`). `factorium outbox [--worker <id>]` answers the record.

e04a653d1535.sentence: Every scenario drives `App` as the CLI does and reads only what the CLI could print (`crates/factorium/tests/scenarios/fixture.rs`).
e04a653d1535.why: how factorium's own tests are written, not what factorium does for a user; held by checks.sh and the scenarios' fixture

e104154232ae.sentence: A new tick step edits `daemon.rs` only.
e104154232ae.why: ADR 0005 describes the module split (which code lives where, what a change edits); none is behaviour a run could break

e1fcaa4d3692.sentence: `run`, `stop`, `service install/remove/show`, `checkout add/remove/list`, `issue add/list/show/edit/close/wait-for-human/ready/start-over/comment/block` (a comment reaches the issue's live worker at once), `doctor`, `discard` (a worker's worktree no open issue owns, as doctor names it), `outbox` (what was passed to a session, and how it went), `workers` (the live ones; `--all`: the ended too), `promote` (now, whatever the bound or a red tip says; while a promotion of that checkout runs, the daemon's or another `promote`, it is refused, its answer naming the running one, and the running one is left be), `cut`, `hold` (landings; `--release` releases them), `unqueue` (a heavy-queue entry that does not move; a running one is ended with every process it started), `heavy run [--background] -- <cmd>` (a program of the owner's that is not a worker queues a heavy command, §1.9; exits with its exit code), `heavy depth` (the queue's depth as JSON: `running`, `waiting`, and each entry), `kit show/set/pin`, `accounts`, `settings`, `help`; hidden, `guard` (the hook a session runs before each tool call)

e4709c8f8169.summary: truefit.toml was changed by 4 fixes in 180 days, and no registered promise's check covers it
e4709c8f8169.why: truefit.toml is the check registry itself: each fix (factorium#186-189) changed it only to register a [[model]] (worktrees, line), re-pin a model's commit, or add covers for new code; the promises those fixes keep live in models/*.tla and the code their covers name, not in this file

e4845e97332c.sentence: launchd does not load it by itself after a reboot: a boot loads no Background agent from ~/Library/LaunchAgents, at boot or at a login, and only root's jobs run before a login (factorium#287). So the first `factorium` command run after the boot loads it, unless `factorium stop` stopped it.

e87d32e6357e.sentence: It may name the **role** its worker plays and the **account** it starts on, as whoever filed it decided (Guild, which keeps roles and accounts' quotas across hosts; guild ADR 0051): a role is a directory, by its absolute path, holding the role's rules (`CLAUDE.md`) and skills (`.claude/skills`), say lore checked out at a rev; its worker starts in a directory of its own whose rules are factorium's worker rules and then the role's, and whose skills are the role's, linked, the role's directory read and never written.

e8a33e699ca0.sentence: Every checkout has a proving branch: one path for every repo.
e8a33e699ca0.why: structure: a checkout is registered with its proving branch; base-moved-only-by-promotion holds the rule

e923ae7a4aa5.sentence: Kept, as afkconvoy decided them: the session file is the turn; the kit orders harnesses and a checkout may pin one; a login that refreshes is bound to one machine (which account a worker starts on is stablehand's pick now, §1.7); admission alone decides each start; the queue starts by the host's CPU reading, never starves, and bounds a hold; hot workers and their evidence; the disk floor and reclaiming `target/`; serial builds (cargo's fine-grain locking opted out); the gate is local, declared, fast and slow, recorded by tree; the proving branch and promotion; the fleet cuts its own versions; the watch, its look, episodes, rounds and report; guards, not identities; the help is the manual.
e923ae7a4aa5.why: a description of the design, its scope or of another system (sunfmin/homebrew-tap, afkconvoy), not a promise a run of factorium could break

e9d3297614e2.sentence: In the ordinary order it waits behind admission's load reading, the heavy queue and its checkout's line, each fair to every issue and none knowing this one matters more.
e9d3297614e2.why: ADR 0015 (urgent, rehomed from the old concepts table): the context line states the problem; the three decisions are held by tests/scenarios/urgent.rs

ea300ca7d549.sentence: **By hand**: `factorium idle <checkout>` runs it now, as `promote` and `cut` move the line now: the steps, then the tasks line, in its own clone at the base's tip, without waiting for an idle host or `every`. It takes the heavy queue's one path at background priority and, as the `tasks_bound` run, yields to nothing but the hold bound: a tick that finds the host busy does not end it, and `unqueue` ends it whole.

ea34d158d387.sentence: `App`'s interface is unchanged: the scenarios and the CLI keep calling the same methods, and `tests/scenarios/binary.rs` tests the binary end to end, so every step is tested as it lands.

eb42a9267d16.sentence: It changes only when how the process runs changes.

eb47ae49457b.sentence: Invariant, as slimfit's: **the Developer ID identity and the notary key live in sunfmin/homebrew-tap only, and only its `release` workflow signs.**

ed046a99c77f.sentence: A worker's or a program's entry that leaves unstarted without the owner taking it off (its waiter refused and failing to exec, or gone) keeps its place for `heavy_keep`: the same worker (or program) asking the same command again within it takes that place, not the back; so a daemon restart or a client that gives up and asks again loses no turn (factorium#193).

ee84ad56b950.sentence: It takes a heavy slot after the lines' moves and the tick's start, so it never goes ahead of a promotion, a cut, a worker's start or a waiting heavy command; it runs beside the ticks, through the heavy queue's one path (its sessions noted on its entry, so `unqueue` ends it whole as it does any running entry, unrecorded), and the first tick that finds the host no longer idle (a worker at work, anything else queued) ends it, unrecorded, to run again in the next idle window, so a worker that wants room waits at most a tick.

f473f0af0031.sentence: That directory's path holds only on this host.

f4743d2d491c.sentence: It is refused when the base declares no `[idle]`, and while idle work of any checkout runs or waits on the host, naming that entry and `factorium unqueue <id>`. **Off on a host**: `[idle]` lives in the repo, so every host with a checkout of it would run it and file the same tasks into its own tracker.

f4cb25b8878b.sentence: The operator's view first answers whether a daemon runs: its pid file names a live process that holds its lock, and that one ticked (`daemon.tick`) within five `tick_every`, never under two minutes.

f785be711f96.sentence: Each `App` method keeps its signature: the CLI and the scenarios call the same interface, so the scenarios are the test of every step.

f7a093f354a1.sentence: What a checkout declares under `[idle]` (§5): steps too slow for any gate (a long soak or load test), run in their own clone at the base's tip while the host is idle — no live worker works (each waits for the watch, or none lives), the heavy queue holds nothing, and the host has room — at most once per `every` (from the last run's start) and within `limit` for all the steps.

f9535c89e20b.sentence: Those public items name no issue, worker, watch or checkout: what only the caller knows it passes in, or says through a trait it implements.

fc1bb0750517.sentence: Doctor answers `decided`: every record, in any issue body or comment (a comment is one only when its first line starts `Decided (`; a line inside a fenced code block, ``` or ~~~, quotes the shape and is none) of any checkout, made since the owner last ran `decided --read`, newest first, each with its checkout and number, who, what, options, chose, undo and when.
